html:
The state oil and gas company of Algeria, founded in 1963, a year after independence. It is the largest company in Africa.

Oil and gas had been found in the Sahara in the 1950s, under French rule, and French companies held the fields when the Algerian War ended in 1962. Sonatrach began by building a pipeline. Under President Houari Boumediene it took over more and more of the industry, and in 1971 Algeria nationalised its oil and gas, taking a majority of the French companies' stakes. Algeria had joined OPEC in 1969.

Oil and gas money paid for Algeria's state-led development, its schools and its army, and it still makes up most of its exports. Gas pipelines run under the Mediterranean to Italy, by way of Tunisia, and to Spain.

The company has also been at the heart of Algerian politics, with several corruption scandals at the top. In 2013 jihadist gunmen seized a gas plant at In Amenas run with foreign partners, and dozens of hostages died.
sum: The state oil and gas company of Algeria, founded in 1963, a year after independence. It is the largest company in Africa.
